questions.question: Which is the Prakrit word for the Sanskrit term ‘dharma’ which means religious duty?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Dhamma**__ is the Prakrit word for the Sanskrit term ‘dharma’ which means religious duty.

• He was the grandson of Chandragupta Maurya.

questions.question: Convex mirror is used as:
questions.solution:
__
 
• Convex mirrors are used as** rear view mirrors in vehicles**__, sunglasses, magnifying glasses, etc.
 
• Convex mirrors are those which have the bulging side facing the light.
 
• The image formed by these mirrors is always virtual and smaller in size.
 
• Concave mirrors are those which are curved inwards. 
 
• They are used in solar cookers, shaving glass, etc.

questions.question: What is the result when a metal is attacked by a substance such as acid?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Corrosion occurs when metals react with acids.**__
 
• When a metal reacts with acids, displacement reaction take place to form a salt and hydrogen gas.
 
• For example, when Sodium (Na) reacts with hydrochloric acid (HCl) then sodium chloride (NaCl) and hydrogen gas (H2) form.
 
• 2 Na (s) + 2 HCl (aq) → 2 NaCl (s) + H2 (g)
 
• Non-metals do not react with acids because non-metals are themselves acceptors of electrons so there is no way they can donate electrons to the hydrogen ion of the acid.

questions.question: When a ray of light is passed through a prism, it splits into his constituent colours. This phenomenon is called:
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Upon passage through the prism, the white light is separated into its component colors - red, orange, yellow, green, blue and violet. The separation of visible light into its different colors is known as dispersion.**__
 
• Visible light, also known as white light, consists of a collection of component colors.
 
• These colors are often observed as light passes through a triangular prism.

questions.question: India’s first specialized hospital for Elephants was opened in:
questions.solution:
__
 
• **India has opened its first specialised hydrotherapy treatment for elephants suffering from arthritis, joint pain and foot ailments in Mathura.**__
 
• The new hydrotherapy jumbo pool has 21 high-pressure jet sprays that create water pressure that massage the elephants’ feet and body.
 
• The facility is run in collaboration with the Uttar Pradesh Forest Department and the NGO Wildlife SOS.
 
• India's first specialised hospital for elephants was formally opened in Mathura on 16 November 2018.
 
• The hospital is located close to the elephant conservation and care centre and is designed to treat injured and sick elephants.
 
• The unique medical centre offers wireless digital X-ray, laser treatment, dental X-ray, thermal imaging, ultrasonography, hydrotherapy and quarantine facilities.

questions.question: Which of the following is not an example of scalar quantity?
questions.solution:
__
 
• Scalar quantities are those which only have magnitude.
 
• Speed, mass, volume, temperature, time, energy, power are examples of scalar quantities.
 
• Vector quantities are those which have both direction and magnitude.
 
• Momentum, **velocity**__, force, acceleration are examples of vector quantities.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a fundamental right?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Right to employment**__ is not a fundamental right.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Fundamental rights are those rights that are basic rights for the life of a person and are provided to the citizens of India by the constitution and which cannot be interfered with by any state.
 
• Indian citizens have the following fundamental rights:-
 
• Right to Equality or Equality (Under Article 14 to Article 18).
 
• Right to freedom (Under Articles 19 to 22).
 
• Right against exploitation (Under Articles 23 to 24).
 
• Right to religious freedom (Under Articles 25 to 28).
 
• Right to Culture as well as Education (Under Articles 29 to 30).
 
• Constitutional Rights (Under Article 32).
